text:
tammy: Heads up — Security plans to land an APAC firewall tightening in ~30m that will restrict outbound to approved KMS/keystore endpoints. I'm worried this will block keystore egress and stop GPU nodes from joining the warmpool. Can we pause the rollout or pre-authorize our endpoints? cc @julian
vikram: who is owning that rollout? link to the PR?
julian: that was me (PR #4523). It's a region-by-region rollout. Scheduled APAC at 15:00. I didn't realise the keystore hostnames we use are served behind dynamic NATs...
olivia: from the last canary: nodes fail to decrypt during bootstrap — logs show `keystore: decrypt error AccessDenied` then `grpc: connection refused`. Looks like egress is blocked to keystore.
tammy: created incident ticket for visibility: INC-2026-APAC-EGRESS (see internal link)
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-APAC-EGRESS created by tammy. Severity: high. Runbook: /runbooks/egress-lockdown. Pager duty: eng-oncall.
vikram: short-term mitigations: 1) add egress allowlist for keystore IP ranges, 2) add SG rule allowing 443 to keystore FQDNs, or 3) rollback the rule. Which is fastest?
julian: rollback is fastest but I prefer a targeted allowlist. Ops — can you add a short-lived egress allowlist for keystore FQDNs used by the GPU fleet (15m window)? We need it live before next batch of nodes starts.
olivia: caveat: keystore egress is NAT'd so the destination IPs seen from nodes are the upstream proxies. We have internal mapping: `keystore.prod.apac -> nat-01.apac-prod (egress IPs: 34.198.12.0/28, 34.198.13.0/28)` but that mapping changes. Suggest using ALB DNS/SNI allow or adding service tag.
toncall: Oncall here — I can push a temporary SG rule: `Type: HTTPS, Port: 443, Destination: sg-keystore-proxies, Description: ephemeral-keystore-mitigation, TTL: 60m`. I'll also tag the change and create a rollback comment.
vikram: also watch conntrack usage on kube nodes — allowing many new outbound connections could spike nf_conntrack. Run `watch -n1 cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` on one staging node before broadening.
julian: ack. I'll revert the APAC deny now to stop further rollout and open a new MR that uses the keystore service-tag rather than a blunt deny. Reverted in 2m.
olivia: after revert, we saw 3 new GPU nodes finish bootstrap successfully within ~4 minutes. Monitoring for errors for 15m.
tammy: agreed plan: julian to submit MR with service-tag-based allowlist, oncall to add temporary SG rule + annotate with tracer tag, ops to enable audit sampling reduction to 10% during the mitigation window to control log volume and cost. If anything spikes, revert to baseline. :lock_with_key:
infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-APAC-EGRESS updated: mitigated via rollback and temporary allowlist. Will auto-close if stable for 2h.
